what_it_does: Designs a low-power serial link receiver for high-speed data transmission (106.25 gigabits per second) using a hybrid equalization approach. High-speed serial connections suffer from signal degradation (channel loss) requiring correction; this receiver uses a feed-forward equalizer (3 taps correcting near-term interference) combined with one tap of decision-feedback equalization (correcting previously decoded bits) to cancel interference without requiring excessive analog-to-digital conversion noise. The approach compensates for 21.2 decibels of channel loss while maintaining low power consumption.
